players.product: silicon and SiC electrodes (cathodes) and rings - etch-chamber consumables

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (DART half-year report, consolidated): revenue KRW 183,487,745,996 against KRW 122,724,680,150 in H1 2025 and operating profit KRW 47,313,528,110 against KRW 17,216,059,339; Q2 alone revenue KRW 90,087,346,644 (Q2 2025: KRW 64,090,378,835) with operating profit KRW 26,015,940,780 (KRW 8,499,384,039). The company says its semiconductor equipment-parts segment posted H1 revenue of KRW 1,823 hundred million, up 49% year on year, and operating profit of KRW 468 hundred million, up 170%. Mix: silicon parts (electrodes and rings, etch-equipment consumables, brand TEL) KRW 163,065M or 88.87% of revenue, other parts (SiC rings, tubes, disks, ingots and others) KRW 19,284M or 10.51%; domestic sales KRW 130,550M and exports KRW 52,938M. H1 R&D spend KRW 4,692M (2.6% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 183,487,745,996 (vs KRW 122,724,680,150); H1 OP KRW 47,313,528,110 (vs KRW 17,216,059,339); Q2 rev KRW 90,087,346,644, Q2 OP KRW 26,015,940,780; parts segment rev KRW 1,823 hundred million (+49%), OP KRW 468 hundred million (+170%); silicon parts KRW 163,065M (88.87%)

quarterly_data.signal: Customers (DART half-year report): main customers are TEL, SEMES and Samsung Electronics in the domestic channel (KRW 129,411M, 70.5% of revenue) and TEL and AMAT in exports (KRW 52,938M, 28.9%); parts are sold through equipment makers to end users or directly. Two unnamed customers each exceeded 10% of revenue in H1 2026: customer A KRW 113,708,102 thousand (share 0.6197) and customer B KRW 42,811,975 thousand (0.2333), against KRW 79,160,491 thousand (0.6450) and KRW 26,150,268 thousand (0.2131) a year earlier. Tokyo Electron Limited holds 13.78% of the company (parent Hana Micron 32.50%). Customers order under master agreements as needed, so there is no long-term order backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A KRW 113,708,102 thousand (0.6197 of revenue), customer B KRW 42,811,975 thousand (0.2333); H1 2025: 0.6450 / 0.2131; Tokyo Electron stake 13.78%
quarterly_data.counterparty: Tokyo Electron, SEMES, Samsung (domestic); Tokyo Electron, Applied Materials (export)

quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material suppliers (DART half-year report): H1 2026 purchases were poly silicon KRW 6,230M (23.1%, from OCI and others) and poly/mono-crystalline ingot KRW 19,656M (72.8%, from MMC and others), KRW 27,012M in total; the average ingot price fell to KRW 141,094/kg from KRW 183,836/kg in FY2025, which the company attributes to changes in imported items and unit prices (poly-crystalline ingot is imported at customers' request). The long-term purchase contract with OCI ended during the half and the company has no long-term purchase contract at period end.
quarterly_data.figure: Poly silicon KRW 6,230M (23.1%, OCI); ingot KRW 19,656M (72.8%, MMC); ingot price KRW 141,094/kg (vs KRW 183,836/kg)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and investment (DART half-year report): silicon-parts production capacity was KRW 125,090M for the half against production of KRW 111,187M, with utilisation of 83.70% (1,881,287 of 2,247,744 available hours) at the Cheonan and Asan sites. H1 facility investment was KRW 10,173M in new/expansion and upgrade equipment for Si and SiC parts; cash purchases of property, plant and equipment were KRW 15,591,489,351 and construction in progress rose to KRW 42,479,989 thousand from KRW 34,503,368 thousand. After the period, on 2026-08-12 the board approved a property, plant and equipment investment with a commitment of KRW 70,200M. The planned industrial-complex expansion next to its plant (originally KRW 320 hundred million) has not started because a cultural-heritage survey is delayed, and its schedule and budget are to be revised.
quarterly_data.figure: Capacity KRW 125,090M, production KRW 111,187M, utilisation 83.70%; H1 capex KRW 10,173M; CIP KRW 42,479,989 thousand; PP&E investment KRW 70,200M approved 2026-08-12
